propositions: Grounding finders flag symbols as missing/unverifiable even when a prerequisite ticket (via depends_on edge) will create them, because they only check the origin/main snapshot and ignore prerequisite ticket content.
The plan-review rubric prose states that symbols created by depended-on tickets should be treated as existing, but this rule is not implemented in the code.

A machine-parseable `<subject> [rebar:<ticket-id>]` citation grammar should be introduced and honored in both a deterministic advisory layer (verifying the edge exists in either direction: P.depends_on(C) or C.blocks(P)) and an LLM layer (judging whether cited ticket C's plan/file_impact provides the relied-upon functionality).
The deterministic citation verification (Layer 1) must never block and must fail closed on any reverse-lookup error, mirroring the existing det_operator_attested advisory pattern.

LLM grounding decisions (Layer 2) must follow a specified protocol: trigger when a missing-functionality finding is about to be emitted for a cited symbol; retrieve the cited ticket; credit the citation (drop the finding) only if the reviewer affirmatively confirms coverage; otherwise the finding stands.

Citations without verified edges, or lacking affirmative LLM coverage confirmation, or unbacked by depends_on/blocks relationships, must never result in wrongful credit and must fail closed to the normal missing-symbol block.
